I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I am 65 now, and my wife and I manage the land ourselves. I finished high school, so I can read fertilizer labels and do the cost calculations, but I also know that what matters is what works on my own field. I don't need a professor to tell me that cotton pulls hard on potassium in August — I have watched the leaves turn yellow for four decades.

My soil is loamy alluvial land. It has decent base fertility, but after years of cotton it gets tired by mid-summer. Last year I applied 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as a base before rotary tilling, then top-dressed with 20 kg per mu of urea at flowering, and added 8 kg per mu of potassium chloride when the bolls started setting. I got 480 kg per mu of seed cotton. That was a solid year, but I think I can push to 520 kg per mu this year if I give the plants a little more potash and irrigate well at flowering.

This year I will keep the same base: 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound, which gives me 7.5 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium right away. At flowering in early July, I will spread 20 kg per mu of urea — that is another 9 kg of nitrogen. When the bolls form in early August, I will add 8 kg per mu of potassium chloride, which is about 5 kg of potassium. That brings my total to about 17 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 12 kg of potassium per mu. That is more fertilizer than some of my neighbors use, but my neighbor Li cut back last year and his yield dropped to 400 kg per mu. I would rather spend an extra 40 yuan per mu on fertilizer than lose 100 kg of cotton.

I have a well, so water is available, but the pump is old and electricity costs money. I will irrigate three times: once before sowing in late April to get good germination, once at flowering in early July, and once at peak boll in mid-August. Three thorough irrigations are enough if I flood the furrows properly. I will not do a fourth unless the drought is severe.

For pests, I spray eight times. I start in mid-June for aphids, then hit the first bollworm generation at the end of June. July is critical — I spray three times in July, spacing them about 10 days apart when the flowers are open. In August I spray twice for spider mites and late bollworm, and once in early September if the fields still look risky. I buy my chemicals from the same dealer in town every year. One spray costs about 25 yuan per mu in chemicals and labor. Eight sprays is 200 yuan per mu. I know some farmers spray 12 or 13 times, but I scout my fields every morning and I know the signs. Eight is enough if you time it right.

I sow Guoxinmian, an improved variety. I buy 3 jin of seed per mu, about 50 yuan. I rotary till in late April because that is what works on this soil — I tried no-tillage once five years ago and the stand was patchy.

My total input cost runs about 850 yuan per mu. If I get 520 kg per mu and the price holds at 7.5 yuan per kg, that is 3,900 yuan revenue per mu. For 5 mu, that is 19,500 yuan gross, about 15,000 yuan after costs. That covers our living expenses and leaves something for repairs. I am not gambling with new methods this year. Last year's system worked, and at my age, steady is better than clever.
